name: Ceibhfhionn

attributes.attribute: spilled the well's water instead of letting humans drink

ate nuts that fell from the hazel trees

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Ceibhfhionn, also known as Cabfin, is an Irish goddess of inspiration. Her place was beside the Well of wisdom. She filled a vessel with its water and then poured it out on the ground, choosing not to let people drink from it. She could represent a human shape of the magic fish that dwelled in that pool. This elusive creature kept wisdom to itself, feeding on the nuts that dropped into the well's water from the enchanted hazel trees.

okr.objective: Ceibhfhionn is the Irish goddess of inspiration who guards the Well of wisdom.
